{{nihongo|'''Washitori Shrine'''|和志取神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Mikawa Province]].

'''Washitori Shrine''' (わしとりじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Nishihongō-chō|Q132044357|qid=Q132044357|lt=Nishihongō-chō}}, {{ill|Okazaki, Aichi|ar|أوكازاكي (آيتشي)|az|Okazaki|azb|اوکازاکی، آیچی|be|Акадзакі|bg|Окадзаки|ca|Okazaki|ce|Окадзаки|ceb|Okazaki (lungsod sa Hapon)|ckb|ئۆکازاکی، ئایچی|cs|Okazaki (Aiči)|de|Okazaki|eo|Okazaki|es|Okazaki (Aichi)|eu|Okazaki (Aichi)|fa|اوکازاکی|fi|Okazaki|fr|Okazaki|ga|Okazaki|gl|Okazaki|hr|Okazaki|hy|Օկաձակի|id|Okazaki|it|Okazaki (Aichi)|ja|岡崎市|kk|Окадзаки|ko|오카자키시|lt|Okadzakis|mdf|Окадзаки|mg|Okazaki|ms|Okazaki, Aichi|mzn|اوکازاکی، آیچی|nl|Okazaki|no|Okazaki|pl|Okazaki|pt|Okazaki|ro|Okazaki|ru|Окадзаки|sh|Okazaki|simple|Okazaki, Aichi|sr|Оказаки|sv|Okazaki|tg|Оказаки|th|โอกาซากิ|tl|Okazaki|tr|Okazaki|tt|Окадзаки|uk|Окадзакі (Айті)|ur|اوکازاکی، ایچی|uz|Okazaki (Aichi)|vi|Okazaki, Aichi|war|Okazaki, Aichi|zh|岡崎市|zh_classical|岡崎市|zh_min_nan|Okazaki-chhī|zh_yue|岡崎|qid=Q242783}}, {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|Q80434|qid=Q80434}}. It is selected as one of the {{ill|Okazaki Tourism Kirari 100 Selections|Q11472991|qid=Q11472991}}<ref>[http://www.city.okazaki.aichi.jp/350/351/p006883_d/fil/1.pdf List of Okazaki Tourism Kirari 100 Selections]</ref>.

=== Overview ===
There are unclear points about its founding, but it is regarded as one of the six ancient shrines of {{ill|Hekikai District|ja|碧海郡|ko|헤키카이군|pl|Powiat Hekikai|zh|碧海郡|qid=Q5368803}} listed in volumes 9 and 10 of the '{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}' {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=register of deities}}. Founding is thought to date back to the Nara period, and a close relation with Ekiya-gō and Tottori relay station in Hekikai District is inferred. In the "Mikawa Kokunai Shinmei Meichō," said to have formed from late {{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}} to {{ill|Kamakura period|Q236205|qid=Q236205}}, it is written as "Junior Fifth Rank Lower, Washitori Tenjin."

The deity is {{ill|Isakiirihikonomiko|ja|五十狭城入彦皇子|zh|五十狹城入彥皇子|qid=Q18700560}}. West of {{ill|Renge-ji|Q24873113|qid=Q24873113|lt=Renge-ji}} in Nishihongō-chō is a kofun called {{ill|Washiyama Kofun|Q28693043|qid=Q28693043}}, said to be the tomb of Isasakiirihiko no Miko.

In {{ill|1870|Q7741|qid=Q7741}} ({{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 3), it was renamed Hasebe Shrine. In May {{ill|1874|Q7761|qid=Q7761}} (Meiji 7), by order of the {{ill|Ministry of Religion (Japan)|Q4294653|qid=Q4294653}}, it was designated Shikinaisha Washitori Shrine, but this was canceled in February {{ill|1875|Q7764|qid=Q7764}} (Meiji 8), returning to the old name. In {{ill|1879|Q7783|qid=Q7783}} (Meiji 12), the shrine name Washitori Shrine was approved as an undecided-style shrine, and on December 28, {{ill|1916|Q2087|qid=Q2087}} ({{ill|Taishō era|Q329174|qid=Q329174}} 5), it was made gōsha.

During early Meiji {{ill|Haibutsu kishaku|Q702298|qid=Q702298}}, Daishi-dō in the precincts moved east. The wooden seated Dainichi Nyorai of Kongōkai and wooden standing Shō-Kanzeon Bosatsu owned by Daishi-dō were designated in the Okazaki City designated cultural properties list on March 30, {{ill|1961|Q3696|qid=Q3696}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|ar|فترة شووا|br|Oadvezh Shōwa|ca|Període Shōwa|cs|Období Šówa|de|Shōwa-Zeit|eo|Ŝova-epoko|es|Era Shōwa|eu|Shōwa aroa|fa|دوره شووا|fi|Shōwa-kausi|fr|Ère Shōwa (1926-1989)|he|תקופת שווה|hi|शोवा युग|hu|Sóva-kor|id|Zaman Shōwa|it|Periodo Shōwa|ja|昭和|ka|შოვას პერიოდი|ko|쇼와 시대|lt|Šiova laikotarpis|ms|Zaman Shōwa|nl|Showaperiode|no|Shōwa-perioden|pl|Shōwa|pt|Período Shōwa|ru|Сёва|simple|Shōwa era|sr|Шова период|sv|Shōwa|th|ยุคโชวะ|tl|Panahong Shōwa|tr|Şova Dönemi|uk|Період Сьова|vi|Thời kỳ Chiêu Hòa|zh|昭和|zh_classical|昭和|zh_min_nan|Chiau-hô|zh_yue|昭和|qid=Q327567}} 36)<ref name="bunkazai">{{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.city.okazaki.lg.jp/1100/1109/1159/p011771.html | title=Okazaki City designated cultural properties list | publisher=Okazaki City website | date=2020-9-8 | accessdate=2021-7-19 }}</ref>.

From Edo through mid-Meiji, this shrine's festival was known as "Omantō" or "Omanto" (meaning horse towers), and fireworks were customary.

Every year, four major festivals are held: Kinen-sai, spring festival, annual festival, and {{ill|Niiname-no-Matsuri|Q11501518|qid=Q11501518}}. In particular, at the autumn Niiname-sai, the sweet-sake festival celebrating good harvests has continued from {{ill|1915|Q2084|qid=Q2084}} (Taishō 4) to today. Pupils of {{ill|Yahagi Nishi Elementary School|Q11472901|qid=Q11472901|lt=Yahagi Nishi Elementary School}} also continue the Urayasu no Mai dance.
